stem:
Crude oil is a mixture of hydrocarbons and provides many useful chemicals when processed.

Two of the stages involved in the processing of crude oil are fractional distillation and cracking.

parts.label: (a)(i)
parts.stem: The diagram is a simplified representation of a fractional distillation column.
parts.text: What has to be done to the crude oil before it enters the column?

parts.label: (a)(ii)
parts.text: What trend in **structure** is there from fraction **A** to fraction **F**?

parts.label: (a)(iii)
parts.text: State the trends in **two** properties of the fractions from **A** to **F**.

parts.label: (b)(i)
parts.stem: The naphtha fraction from fractional distillation of crude oil is used as a starting material for cracking.
parts.text: Write an equation for the cracking of $\text{C}_{12}\text{H}_{26}$ to form the products ethene and one other hydrocarbon in a 2:1 mole ratio.

parts.label: (b)(ii)
parts.text: Suggest a use for each of the products from your equation in **(i)**. Explain what makes each product from **(i)** suitable for the use you suggest.

parts.label: (c)(i)
parts.stem:
Burning hydrocarbons can cause a number of environmental problems.

The products of internal combustion engines can include oxides of nitrogen and oxides of carbon.

Sulfur dioxide is a by-product of burning coal in power stations.
parts.text: Explain how and why oxides of nitrogen are produced in internal combustion engines.

parts.label: (c)(ii)
parts.text: Write an equation for the reaction between nitrogen monoxide and carbon monoxide in a catalytic converter.

parts.label: (c)(iii)
parts.text: Write equations to show the involvement of nitrogen monoxide in the formation of acid rain from atmospheric sulfur dioxide.

parts.label: (c)(iv)
parts.text: Describe two of the problems associated with acid rain.
